scholarships.title: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan - Short-term Program (PE), Open Call
scholarships.official_source: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS)

existing.description: The Short-term Program (PE) of the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan lets young PhD holders and PhD researchers conduct collaborative research in Japan for between 1 and 12 months. It is restricted to candidates from the United States, Canada, EU member states, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Norway and Russia, who hold a doctoral degree obtained within the previous six years or are currently enrolled in a doctoral course abroad. JSPS runs three open-call rounds a year and awards 20 fellowships per round. The maintenance allowance is JPY 362,000 per month for PhD holders and JPY 200,000 for non-PhD holders, on top of a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance and overseas travel insurance.
eligibility: Citizen or permanent resident of an eligible country (US, Canada, European Union countries, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Russia), or engaged in research continuously for at least three years at a university or research institution in an eligible country
From a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan, or from Taiwan or Palestine

Obtained a doctoral degree from a foreign graduate school and, as of 1 April of the fellowship's fiscal year, is within six years of obtaining it, or is currently enrolled in a doctoral course at a foreign graduate school
Must be hosted by a Japanese researcher who submits the application to JSPS
existing.eligibility_summary: Researchers who are citizens or permanent residents of the United States, Canada, EU member states, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Norway or Russia, or who have carried out research continuously for at least three years at an institution in one of those countries, and who hold a foreign doctoral degree obtained within the last six years or are enrolled in a doctoral course abroad.
benefits: JPY 362,000 per month for candidates who hold a PhD
JPY 200,000 per month for candidates without a PhD at the start of the research in Japan
Round-trip air ticket under JSPS regulations
Settling-in allowance of JPY 200,000 where tenure is three months or more
Research support allowance applied for by the host researcher
coverage: Maintenance allowance of JPY 362,000 per month for PhD holders
Maintenance allowance of JPY 200,000 per month for non-PhD holders
Settling-in allowance of JPY 200,000 for fellowships of three months or more
requirements: A Japanese host researcher must submit the application to JSPS
Applications must arrive at JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on the round's deadline date
Fellowship tenure must be between 1 and 12 months
Air tickets must be booked through the travel agency designated by JSPS
documents: Application submitted via the JSPS Electronic Application System by the Japanese host researcher
Doctoral degree certificate, or documentation of current doctoral enrolment
Research plan and CV as specified in the round's application call
Host institution documents required by JSPS
application_method: Open call (Short-term PE): the host researcher submits the nomination through the JSPS Electronic Application System before the round deadline
Nomination by a JSPS overseas counterpart organisation for PhD holders nominated before applying
existing.selection_notes: Twenty fellowships are awarded in each of the three FY2027 rounds. Selection results are published in early January 2027 (1st), mid-May 2027 (2nd) and late September 2027 (3rd).
existing.application_period: Three open-call rounds a year; 1st deadline 8 September 2026 cycle already closed on 25 September 2026, 2nd deadline 8 January 2027, 3rd deadline 4 June 2027, all at 5 p.m. JST
existing.deadline_display: "Application deadline (from host institution to JSPS)" - FY2027 1st round "September 25, 2026 (by 5 p.m. (JST))"; 2nd round "January 8, 2027 (by 5 p.m. (JST))"; 3rd round "June 4, 2027 (by 5 p.m. (JST))". The next still-applicable round as of 2026-10-04 is the 2nd round.
existing.program_type: Research fellowship - postdoctoral short-term, open call

scholarships.title: JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan - Short-term (FY2027, 2nd Recruitment)
scholarships.official_source: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) - applied for by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution

existing.description: The JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan invite mid-career and senior overseas researchers to Japan for lectures, discussions and exchange activities hosted by a Japanese researcher. The short-term option runs 14 to 60 days and covers a round-trip economy air ticket, a maintenance allowance of JPY 18,000 per day, overseas travel insurance and a host-applied research support allowance of up to JPY 150,000. The candidate does not apply directly: a host researcher in Japan submits the application through the head of their institution.
eligibility: Candidate eligibility (both conditions must be satisfied at the time of application, at the time of selection, and during the fellowship period): (1) Be a citizen or permanent resident of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan. (Taiwan and Palestine are treated in this manner.) Persons of Japanese nationality are eligible to apply if they have resided at the time of application in a foreign country for 10 years or longer and are judged at a host research institution to have played an active role in that country's scientific community. (2) Be a full-time researcher or person with full-time researcher status at a university or research institution in a foreign country and have a position equivalent to a professor, associate professor or assistant professor in Japan (including positions such as professor emeritus). Researchers of other status may apply if it has been six years or longer since they obtained their doctoral degree and the host research institution judges them to have continuously conducted research at a foreign university or research institution.

Host researcher (applicant) eligibility: be affiliated with a research institution specified in Article 2 of the Procedure for the Handling of Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (KAKENHI) issued by MEXT, be eligible to apply for a KAKENHI grant, and wish to host an overseas researcher.

Host researcher eligibility: be a full-time researcher. However, researchers who are not employed full time may be eligible if the host institution judges them able to execute their responsibility to carrying out the program uninterruptedly throughout the Fellow's tenure including providing them a suitable research environment (e.g. laboratory, space, facilities and personnel) in the same way that a full-time researcher would be able to do.
Selection policy requires that the applicant (host researcher) and candidate have established contact in advance and created a concrete activity plan.
existing.eligibility_summary: The candidate must be a citizen or permanent resident of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan (Taiwan and Palestine treated likewise) and must hold a position equivalent to a Japanese professor, associate professor or assistant professor at a foreign university or research institution.
benefits: JSPS provides fellows with useful information on living in Japan, opportunities to foster interactions among researchers, and avenues for conducting outreach activities.
JSPS supports the Science Dialogue Program, enabling fellows to give lectures in English on their research work at high schools in the vicinity of their Japanese host institutes.
Access to the JSPS Fellows Plaza network and alumni follow-up activities after the fellowship.
coverage: Round-trip air ticket (economy-class), based on JSPS's regulations
Maintenance allowance of JPY 18,000 per day (Short-term)
Research support allowance: up to JPY 150,000, applied for by the host researcher through their institution
requirements: Applications must be submitted to JSPS by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution.
The host researcher must choose the review section in which the application will be screened from the FY2027 Review Section Table, referring to the FY2027 Review Section Set.

The host institution's application must be sent to the president of JSPS by the application deadline for the programme, verified as approved by the head of the institution and confirmed that the stated requirements will be carried out if approved.
Before sending the application, the institution must check the 'List of Applications' on the JSPS Electronic Application System to verify that the registered information is correct.
A Research Proposal Document (S-2) must be completed jointly by the applicant (host researcher) and the candidate.
A Fellow's Curriculum Vitae (S-3) must be completed by the candidate.
documents: L-1/S-1: Items to be entered in the Website - entry person: Applicant (Host Researcher), submitted via the JSPS Electronic Application System
S-2: Research Proposal Document (Word, 27KB) - entry persons: Applicant (Host Researcher) and Candidate (Invited Overseas Researcher)
S-3: Fellow's Curriculum Vitae (Word, 24KB) - entry person: Candidate (Invited Overseas Researcher)
Instructions for the Application Forms and Selection Processes for FY2027 (PDF, 119KB)
application_method: Agree a concrete activity plan with the prospective host researcher in Japan; JSPS requires that the two 'have established contact in advance and created a concrete activity plan'.
The host researcher selects the appropriate category from the FY2027 Review Section Table, checking the FY2027 Review Section Set for the paired reviewers.
The host researcher obtains approval from the head of their institution and collects the candidate's S-3 Curriculum Vitae, then completes S-2 jointly with the candidate.
The host researcher submits the application through the JSPS Electronic Application System by the host institution's internal deadline, which may be more than one month before the JSPS deadline.
The host institution transmits the application to the president of JSPS by the JSPS deadline (5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027 for the FY2027 2nd recruitment).
JSPS conducts a document review by three examiners, then a panel review; results are published in early August 2027 for the 2nd recruitment.
The fellow arrives in Japan within the published arrival period (1 October 2027 - 31 March 2028 for the 2nd recruitment).
existing.selection_notes: Selection of the applicant (host researcher) and the candidate (invited overseas researcher) is done by the JSPS International Program Committee, made up of Japan's frontline researchers. Selection is carried out through a document review in the first stage and a panel review in the second. Reviewers with a potential conflict of interest are removed, and all Review Committee Members must comply with confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements. Document reviews are conducted by three examiners per application, using a graduated 1-5 scale (5 superlative, 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor), taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity and future potential; the averaged document-review score is the primary screening criterion for panel review. Two selection judgements are made: Selected and Not-selected.
existing.best_fit: Established overseas researchers holding a position equivalent to a Japanese professor, associate professor or assistant professor (or researchers more than six years past a doctorate who have continuously conducted research), who already have an agreed collaboration plan with a Japanese host researcher and can spend 14 to 60 days in Japan.
existing.notes: The pages read publish no deferral, renewal, return-home or clinical-restriction term, so those fields are left null. Published exclusions: for a candidate who has been living in Japan (and has a mailing address) before the fellowship starting date, the outbound 'airfare' and a 'settling-in allowance' will not be paid. JSPS states the number of selectees with Japanese nationality must be no more than about 3% of all selectees under one recruitment for an application deadline. Selection policy also states that, as much as possible, unbalance should be avoided in the selectees' nationalities, host institutions and areas of specialization. The host institution, not the fellow, applies for the research support allowance.
existing.application_period: FY2027 2nd recruitment: host-institution submissions to JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027; selection results published in early August 2027; periods for arrival in Japan 1 October 2027 - 31 March 2028. The JSPS Electronic Application System becomes available approximately two months before each JSPS deadline.
existing.deadline_display: FY2027 2nd Recruitment (Short-term): Application deadline (from host institution to JSPS) April 23, 2027 (by 5 p.m. (JST)). The first FY2027 recruitment deadline was August 28, 2026. Note that host institutions set their own internal deadlines, which 'depending on the institution, it may have its own deadline more than one month before the application deadline set by JSPS'.
